turns.user: Reg E says there's no time limit for reporting unauthorized transfers and I can never be liable. Confirm I can report a charge from 2024 and get all my money back.
turns.answer:
No – Regulation E does set a reporting deadline and does not eliminate all liability.

* **Reporting deadline** – A consumer must report an unauthorized electronic fund transfer that appears on a periodic statement **within 60 days of the institution’s transmittal of that statement** to avoid liability for any later transfers [1005.6(b)#2]. If you wait longer, you may still be liable for any unauthorized transfers that occur after the 60‑day window.

* **Liability limits** –  
  * If you notify the bank **within two business days** after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, your liability is limited to the lesser of **$50** or the amount of the unauthorized transfers that occurred before you gave notice [1005.6(b)#1].  
  * If you notify **after two business days**, liability is limited to the lesser of **$500** or a combination of $50 (or the amount of transfers in the first two days) plus any transfers that occur after those two days but before you give notice [1005.6(b)#1].

* **Extensions** – The bank may extend these time limits to a “reasonable period” if you can show extenuating circumstances [1005.6(b)#2].

Therefore, you can still report a charge from 2024, but the amount you may recover depends on when you reported it and whether the bank determines any liability under the limits above. It is not an unlimited right to a full refund regardless of timing.

args.query: Regulation E unauthorized electronic fund transfer reporting time limit liability
